model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity on tangible book (engine route)

equity_bridge.item: Series E 4.70% noncumulative perpetual preferred stock (liquidation preference)
equity_bridge.note: Senior to common; deducted at par rather than charging the $41.8M/yr dividend to the flows. Backed out of FY2025 preferred dividends 41.8 / 4.70% coupon; XBRL carries no PreferredStockValue tag.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case FY2027-FY2031 average revenue growth (4.0-5.0%); equity CAGR rejected as the anchor because NTRS pays out ~100% of earnings (110% in FY2025), which mechanically suppresses book growth without saying anything about earnings power
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 2.1% vs revenue 5.8% and EPS 9.9% - divergence >30%. Cause is distribution policy (buybacks shrank the diluted count from 208.3M to 192.2M over FY2020-25 and AOCI moved from positive to -590.5M), not a deteriorating franchise. EPS CAGRs are flattered at the 3-yr point by FY2022's low base (6.16) and by buybacks; revenue CAGRs are clean of the FY2024 Visa gain because FY2025 is the end point.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are computed on NET INCOME (the FCFE proxy: FY2025 1,736.9 vs FY2022 1,336.0 vs FY2020 1,209.3), not on the CSV's reported FCF, which is deposit-flow noise for a bank (FY2024 -587.5, FY2025 +5,459.5). Revenue: FY2025 8,086.4 / FY2022 6,761.2 / FY2020 6,100.8. EPS: 8.78 / 6.16 / 5.48. Equity: 12,957.9 / 11,259.5 / 11,688.3. All FY-end December.

scenario_narratives.base: Northern Trust's value turns on three axes: (1) organic trust-fee growth on AUC/A of $17.4T and wealth AUC of $1.3T, which the base case holds at mid-single digits as market levels compound and alternatives/family-office mandates add net new business (eight straight quarters of positive organic fee growth); (2) net interest income, ~27% of revenue, which gives back some of 2026's NIM expansion (1.81% in Q2-26) as the Fed eases, netting revenue growth to 4-5% through FY2031 and 3% thereafter; (3) operating leverage, where the restructuring programme and management's ~400bps FY2026 target lift the pretax margin from 32% to 33% - the level NTRS already achieved in FY2018-19 - rather than to BNY's mid-30s. Capital retention runs at 0.8x growth, so ~90% of earnings is distributed through the $0.80 quarterly dividend and buybacks. FY2027 is modelled as a soft year (+4%, 50bps margin give-back) because 2026 revenue was lifted by a 69% jump in capital-markets income that management itself expects to moderate.
scenario_narratives.bull: Fee growth stays high-single-digit as the alternatives-servicing and ultra-high-net-worth franchises take share and equity markets keep compounding; capital-markets and securities-lending income holds near the 2026 level instead of mean-reverting; the restructuring charges convert into durable cost savings so the 2026 operating-leverage run-rate persists and the pretax margin reaches 35% by FY2031. Lower capital intensity (0.7x growth) and a stable 12% CET1 let payout stay ~100%. The scarcity value of being one of three scaled global custodians (BNY Mellon's 2025 approach) is NOT separately priced - it is upside to this case, not inside it.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2026 air-pocket risk materialises in FY2027: capital-markets and securities-lending revenue falls a quarter from cyclically high levels, Fed easing compresses NIM faster than deposit growth offsets it, and flat equity markets stall ad-valorem fee growth, so revenue drops 2% against a sticky cost base and the pretax margin falls to FY2023's ~28%. Basel III endgame lands at the unfavourable end (RWA +10%), forcing ~$130M/yr of extra retention in FY2027-28 and curtailing buybacks; the sub-scale franchise then grows only 2.5-3% with the margin recovering to 30%, and the market exits at 13x FCFE. No solvency or going-concern element - this is a de-rating and an earnings reset, not a credit event.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Northern Trust is a fee-led trust and custody bank that distributes essentially all of its earnings, so it is valued as a stream of free cash flow to equity (net income less the capital retained to grow risk-weighted assets at a ~12% CET1) capitalised at a 9.75% USD cost of equity, with deposits and wholesale funding treated as operating liabilities and only the $885M preferred deducted ahead of common. FY0 is the FY2026 guided run-rate with the Visa gain, the securities loss and the restructuring charges stripped out, so the valuation does not capitalise a one-off. The three cases differ on where capital-markets income settles after 2026, how much of the 2026 operating leverage is structural, and how much capital Basel III endgame absorbs.
key_risks_to_valuation: Net interest income (~27% of revenue) is the swing factor: a faster or deeper Fed easing cycle than guidance assumes compresses NIM from the 1.81% Q2-26 level and takes FY2027 revenue growth negative, as in the bear case
2026 capital-markets, FX and securities-lending income (+69% YoY in Q2) is cyclically elevated; the base case already assumes moderation, but a sharp reversal produces the FY2027 air-pocket
Ad-valorem trust fees make ~55% of revenue directly sensitive to equity and bond market levels; a 20% market drawdown would cut fee revenue high-single-digits with a lag
Basel III endgame could lift RWAs 5-15%, raising the capital retention the model charges (bear case uses 1.3x growth plus a two-year CET1 rebuild) and reducing buyback capacity
Restructuring charges (~$220M in Q2-26) must convert into durable cost savings; if the efficiency programme stalls, the base case's 33% pretax margin is not reached

The model holds the share count flat and treats buybacks as the FCFE distribution channel; the per-share value is therefore insensitive to the pace of repurchases but sensitive to the 25.5% tax rate and 9.75% cost of equity (see sensitivity grid)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 121.12-195.78
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 0000073124): FY2025 10-K filed 2026-02-24 and Q2-2026 10-Q filed 2026-07-30 for revenue components, noninterest expense, pretax income, tax, preferred dividends, D&A, software/premises capex, buybacks, dividends, goodwill, AOCI, deposits and share counts; NTRS_Metrics.csv (XBRL-derived) for the FY2007-FY2025 history
data_sources.qualitative: NTRS_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): Q2-2026 results and raised FY2026 guidance (NII and revenue +9-10%, ~400bps operating leverage), notable items, CET1 trajectory, Basel III endgame and rate-sensitivity risks, BNY Mellon 2025 approach

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY0 = FY2026E total revenue (NII + noninterest income) EX-NOTABLES, built from H1-2026 actuals (NII 1,329.5 + noninterest income 3,574.2 = 4,903.7, less the $525.0M Visa Class B exchange gain, plus the $73.9M AFS securities repositioning loss = 4,452.6 underlying, +13.1% YoY) and management's raised FY2026 guidance of +9-10% revenue growth; 8,880 is +9.8% on FY2025's 8,086.4 and sits at the top half of the range because H1 annualises to 8,905. Same FY0-run-rate convention as NAB.AX. FY2025 actual revenue 8,086.4 (XBRL Revenues tag; NII 2,411.0 + noninterest income 5,675.4).
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 10-Q cover-page common shares outstanding 182,955,653 (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding, filed 2026-07-30, post Q2 buybacks) plus 0.90M dilutive share-based awards (Q2-2026 IncrementalCommonSharesAttributableToShareBasedPaymentArrangements 896,274). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed inside noninterest expense; buybacks (FY2025 $1,273.5M, H1-2026 $709.5M) are the distribution mechanism for FCFE, not a modelled count reduction.
inputs.net_debt_note: Bank convention (house precedent NAB.AX, HBAN, GL): deposits ($145.6B), other borrowings ($8.6B) and senior/subordinated notes ($3.3B) are operating funding of a deposit-taker and are already serviced inside net interest income; FCFE is post-interest, so net debt is held at 0 and the flows are capitalised at the cost of equity. The only claim senior to common deducted is the $885M Series E preferred (equity_bridge).
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is the FY2026E FCFE proxy: net income ex-notables 2,117 (pretax 2,842 at a 32.0% margin, 25.5% tax) less 696 of capital retention at 0.8 x the 9.8% FY2026 revenue growth. reported_fcf is the CSV's FY2025 OCF-less-capex (5,459.5) and is deposit-flow noise for a bank (FY2024 was -587.5 on the same business); it is recorded for auditability only and the owner-FCF identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income deliberately does NOT hold on this route.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense FY2025 = $126.5M (1.56% of revenue); no separate equity-award tax figure published - net-share-settlement withholding (450k shares FY2025) is treated as part of the buyback cash. SBC is already inside noninterest expense, so the pretax margin is post-SBC; sbc_pct_path is carried explicitly so the engine's house/street band is computed.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income IS the business for a bank (NII 2,411 FY2025). Nothing is added back as net cash, so there is no double count.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock $1,273.5M plus common dividends $591.6M = $1,865M returned vs $1,695M net income to common (110% payout; CET1 was above target). H1-2026: buybacks $709.5M + dividends $295.4M. Quarterly dividend $0.80 ($3.20 annualised, 1.9% yield at the current price).
inputs.fy0_note: FY0 is the FY2026 guided ex-notables estimate (fiscal year closes 31 Dec 2026, nine months elapsed at the valuation date), so Y1 = FY2027. Last fully reported year is FY2025.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-06-30 balance sheet; cover-page count as of the 10-Q filed 2026-07-30

balance_sheet_anchors.cet1_ratio_note: CET1 ~12.0% at Q1-2026 (12.6% at YE2025) per Analysis.json; management operating range ~11-12%
balance_sheet_anchors.note: Preferred carrying value is not tagged in XBRL; $885M is backed out of the $41.8M/yr preferred dividend at the Series E 4.70% coupon (41.8 / 0.047 = 889) and matches the known $885M Series E issue.

inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 9.75% in USD: 10-yr UST ~4.25%, equity risk premium 5.0%, beta ~1.1 for a custody/trust bank (higher operating leverage to market levels and rates than a retail bank, no credit-cycle balance sheet to speak of). Single rate across all three scenarios so risk is charged once, through the probability weights, not through per-scenario discount rates. Labelled 'wacc' only because that is the engine's field name; no debt is in the capital structure being discounted.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (premises) are expensed inside noninterest expense and therefore inside the pretax margin; no lease liability is added to net debt and no separate lease line is carried (treatment A, applied once).
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; net income is fully attributable to the parent.
inputs.engine_mapping: The component engine is driven as a bank P&L: 'EBITDA margin' = pretax-income margin + D&A % + SBC %, so that EBITDA - SBC - D&A = pretax income; cash_tax_rate 25.5% (FY2025 effective 25.8%, H1-2026 25.4%) turns that into net income; da_pct and capex_pct share an 8.8% core (FY2025 depreciation/amortisation/accretion 779.1 vs software 700.2 + premises 74.0 = 774.2 of capex, i.e. D&A ~= capex), and the EXCESS of capex_pct over da_pct is the capital retained to fund balance-sheet growth at a ~12% CET1 - retention = k x revenue growth, with k = 0.8 base / 0.7 bull / 1.3 bear (TCE/revenue is ~1.32x, so k = 1.3 assumes RWA grows one-for-one with revenue; 0.8 reflects that roughly half of NTRS's growth is ad-valorem fee growth on AUC/A that consumes no RWA - over FY2019-25 tangible common grew ~1.5%/yr against ~4%/yr underlying revenue growth with a ~95% average payout). Working-capital capture is 0. The resulting flow is FCFE = net income - retained capital, capitalised at the cost of equity, and the Series E preferred is deducted in the bridge instead of its $41.8M dividend being deducted from the flows (par deduction is the more conservative of the two at a 9.75% cost of equity).
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE at cost of equity, through the component engine route - the routing table's bank row (residual income on tangible book) implemented as the house precedent for HBAN, NAB.AX and GL does it: net_debt = 0, preferred deducted in equity_bridge, retention tied to growth. BVPS-compounding was rejected because NTRS distributes ~100% of earnings (book has compounded at 2%/yr while EPS compounded at 10%), so book is not the value driver - distributable earnings are. An owner-FCF DCF was rejected because OCF swings from -486 (FY2024) to +5,534 (FY2025) on deposit flows. SBC: expensed (inside noninterest expense) and share count held flat; funded by a real buyback programme. FY0 ANCHOR: FY2026E ex-notables (revenue 8,880, pretax margin 32.0%, net income 2,117, EPS ex-notables ~$11.3 on 183.9M diluted shares - 15.0x at the current price). Notables excluded from FY0: +$525.0M Visa Class B exchange gain (Q2-26 noninterest income), -$73.9M AFS securities repositioning loss (Q2-26), -~$220M restructuring (severance, software write-offs, one-time equity grants, Q2-26 noninterest expense). H1-2026 underlying pretax margin was 34.5%; FY0 at 32.0% assumes H2 normalises as management guided (full-year operating leverage ~400bps vs 700bps+ in Q2). DATA FLAG for the parent: the CSV's interim 'Revenue' rows (Q1-2026 1,341.4, Q2-2026 1,349.5, H1-2026 2,690.9) are the ASC-606 trust-fee subset, not total revenue (true Q1-2026 = NII 654.0 + noninterest income 1,551.6 = 2,205.6) - the same XBRL tag-preference trap recorded for HBAN; the FY rows (6,464.5 ... 8,086.4) are correct totals. CSV EPS is basic (FY2025 8.78) where diluted is 8.74. Tax: 25.5% flat - FY2025's rate included a 2.6pp valuation-allowance item, so the underlying ~25% plus state/foreign gives 25.5%; no NOL or credit ramp is needed.

bear.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied pretax margin [28.5, 28.0, 28.5, 29.0, 29.5, 30.0, ...]: FY2027 revenue falls 2% (capital markets/securities lending -25% from the 2026 peak, NIM compression as the Fed eases, flat market levels) while the cost base is sticky, so the margin drops to FY2023's ~28% and recovers only to 30%.
bear.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = 1.3 x revenue growth (RWA grows one-for-one with revenue) plus 1.5% of revenue in FY2027-28 (~$130M/yr) to rebuild CET1 against a Basel III endgame RWA uplift of 5-15%; terminal cap 13x FCFE reflects a de-rated, slower-growing trust bank.

base.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied pretax margin = EBITDA - SBC - D&A = [31.5, 32.0, 32.5, 33.0, 33.0, ...]: FY2027 dips 50bps from FY0's 32.0% as capital-markets/securities-lending revenue normalises from the 2026 peak, then ~400bps/yr operating leverage targets lift it to 33%, NTRS's own FY2018-19 level, by FY2030 and hold there.
base.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = 0.8 x revenue growth = [3.2, 4.0, 4.0, 3.6, 3.6, 3.2, 3.2, 2.8, 2.4, 2.4]% of revenue; terminal retention 2.4% of revenue is ~10% of net income, i.e. a ~90% payout at 3% growth, matching NTRS's FY2019-25 average.
base.terminal_note: Cap 15x FCFE (~13x net income) is the exit a buyer of a mature trust bank plausibly pays (NTRS 10-yr forward P/E range ~11-17x); Gordon at 9.75%/3.0% is 15.3x so the cap binds marginally.

bull.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied pretax margin [33.0, 33.5, 34.0, 34.5, 35.0, 35.0, ...]: the 2026 operating-leverage run-rate is sustained (restructuring savings land, trust-fee growth stays high-single-digit), reaching a BNY-like 35% pretax margin.
bull.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = 0.7 x revenue growth: more of the growth is capital-light fee growth (alternatives servicing, family-office wealth), so less CET1 is consumed per dollar of revenue.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because the Analysis flags interest-rate sensitivity as the single high-severity risk, FY2026 earnings are visibly flattered by one-offs (Visa gain) and by capital-markets income management itself expects to normalise, and Basel III endgame is an unresolved regulatory overhang that has already dented CET1 (12.6% to ~12%). Bull cut to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right at once - sustained peak capital-markets income, durable restructuring savings, and benign rates - and consensus sits at Hold with targets only mid-single-digits above the price. Takeover optionality (BNY 2025 approach, management committed to independence) is noted but not weighted.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
